doc_intro: What the numbers, grades, smileys and buttons mean. Technology and measuring methods in detail are in the project's README.
doc_nav: Grades and colours · Stickers · Metrics · Deck baseline · Second opinion and audit · Groove skips · Tracks · Copies and history · Comparison · Learning · Condition and findings · Operation · Limits
doc_grades_p1: The scale follows Goldmine (Discogs): NM near mint, VG+ played but sonically clean, VG audible defects begin, G+ clearly impaired but usable, G heavily worn, still plays through, F skips or sticks. Goldmine gives no numbers, only descriptions; our limits are starting values that are refined by ear.
doc_grades_p2: The overall grade comes from the music: clicks and pops per minute while music plays (confirmed by the second opinion), and pops per minute over the whole side; the worse of the two counts. Limits for clicks in the music: NM up to 3, VG+ up to 10, VG up to 20, G+ up to 40, G up to 80 per minute. Clicks and crackle in the pauses (above the deck baseline) get grades of their own and lower the overall grade by at most one step, and only when they are at least two steps worse. Lead-in and run-out groove never count, noise is for information only. F is only given when the stylus skips back. Clipping: 5 s after the stylus drop and before the lift, and everything after the end of the music, do not count; from 200 samples in the music it is noted in the recording, from 500 there is no grade (recording error). The three values are in the settings under “Clipping” and apply to new analyses.
doc_grades_p3: Colours: NM green, VG+ olive, VG amber, G+ orange, G orange-red, F red; from Discogs additionally M emerald and P burgundy.
doc_stickers_p: The record grade per copy is the average of the sides: per side the latest graded recording, then the mean of the grade steps (NM + VG = VG+); half steps go to the worse grade (NM + VG+ = VG+). If one side skips (F), the record is F. If only one side was measured, this is noted. The same grade appears in the record list and goes into the Discogs collection. The smiley appears next to every measured grade; name and colour on hover.
doc_measures_tick: Crackle (tick): a spike that stands out from the groove noise and is a thin line in the spectrogram, with a strength below 25. Strength = peak divided by what is normal at that spot. Barely audible on its own, in large numbers the crackle of a pause.
doc_measures_click: Click: the same from strength 25 on, a single audible click.
doc_measures_pop: Pop: a click that is also loud in absolute terms (at the level of the profile's reference tone); it comes through even in the middle of the music.
doc_measures_rates: Clicks/min quiet: clicks and pops per minute in pauses, lead-in and lead-out. Crackle/min: crackle there. Clicks music: clicks and pops in the music. Pops/min: over the whole side.
doc_measures_raw_net: In tables the raw value comes first, in brackets the value above the deck baseline; the grade uses the value in brackets.
doc_measures_noise: Noise: level of the quiet passages, also relative to the music. On some turntables the signal chain sets this value rather than the record, so it is only shown as a single value.
doc_measures_scratch: Scratch: a click that repeats every revolution (±0.6 %, at least 4 revolutions). Several chains close together are usually one physical scratch across several grooves.
doc_baseline_p: When setting up a turntable, the app counts clicks and crackle per minute in the silent groove of the test record (side 2). That is what the chain brings along: stylus, cartridge, dust, static charge. Every record side is rated minus this baseline, so that two turntables become comparable. If the baseline is higher than what good records show, the test record was dirty or charged during setup: record side 2 again after using an anti-static brush, and the baseline is updated.
doc_ai_p1: The AI column is the click probability from the grooveclean network (MIT licence), queried only for our clicks and pops; from 55 % on it counts as “confirmed”. The network gives a hint, it is not the judge: the grade uses our counts.
doc_ai_p2: Audit: in the event list ▶ listen and judge: Click (confirmed, counts), False alarm (the music itself, e.g. an attack, a snare, a plucked string; not a click), unclear (stays as detected). “False alarm” drops out of count, grade and scratch search at once and is kept when re-analyzing. The verdicts are the training material for a classifier of our own. “Play only the clicks” plays the difference track: only what was counted, silence in between; if you hear music in it, it is a false alarm.
doc_skips_p: If a revolution repeats, the stylus has skipped back (skip → F). Hits with low similarity or an imprecise period are “uncertain” and do not count; they are usually rhythm or a loop. The run-out groove is detected and listed as “run-out groove”. If the detection is wrong, judge it in the skip table: Run-out groove or no skip; the counts are updated at once. The run-out automatic stops the recording after three revolutions in the run-out groove.
doc_tracks_p: If Discogs has track durations for the pressing, the analysis places the track boundaries from the start of the music according to the durations, scaled to the measured music length, and moves each boundary to the nearest pause found. Per track: clicks without crackle per minute, crackle, pops, scratches, share confirmed by the AI, play button. Without durations there is no table.
doc_copies_p: If you own the same record more than once, enter “Copy 1”, “Copy 2” when recording (spelling does not matter). The recordings table then sorts by copy (with a dividing line in between), within a copy by date. The record list shows the grade per copy, and the “Copies” block on the record page gives a verdict: per side the latest recording of each copy, compared by grade, then clicks in pauses, then in the music. The history per side shows every recording as a step with the percentage change from the previous one; “n/a” appears when turntable or level do not match.
doc_compare_p: Two recordings of the same side are overlaid with sample accuracy. Clicks at the same spot (±4 ms) have remained (physical damage), those only in the first are removed (dirt), those only in the second are new. Two uncleaned recordings show the measurement uncertainty. Different sides or records cannot be compared; after a wash, loose dust moves around, so many clicks are “different”, while permanent ones remain.
doc_learning_p: The system learns from every master comparison (the master tells for each detection whether it is music or only on the vinyl) and from your verdicts (click, false alarm). From this it estimates for each recording how many of the reported clicks are real: in the recordings table “≈” next to music/min, in the report “estimated real”, in the event list the column “real?”. It does not sort out single detections, it is not reliable enough for that; but the total is accurate (on real test pressings, crackle within ±5 % instead of +52 %). Settings → Learning shows how well the estimate has been verified per type; the grade can also be computed from the estimate there. That only pays off once a second record with a master is included. Every record with a master and every verdict makes it better, verdicts on records without a master most of all, and both kinds: confirm real clicks as “click” too.
doc_condition_p: Condition of the recording: uncleaned, after wet cleaning, after dry cleaning, other. In addition the cleaning method as free text, findings as checkboxes (visible scratch, hairline scratch, warp, dirt, fingerprints, off-center hole) and a note. Everything can be changed later in the recording. The findings belong to the record, not to the recording: they apply per copy and side, and all recordings of that copy side show them. They are set in the report of a recording (“Report” in the recordings table), and changing them there changes them for all recordings of that copy side. Condition, cleaning and note stay per recording. Changing side and condition: double-click the side or the condition in the recordings table (double-tap on a phone), confirm, then Enter or the selection saves, Esc cancels. A different side re-analyzes the recording (the tracks come from Discogs per side).
doc_op_preview: Preview: listen to the turntable in the browser without recording (starts the level check as well). While recording, the button is called Monitor and can rewind.
doc_op_graphs: Graphs: drag = zoom, double-click = whole side, click = listen, hovering plays the click under the pointer (switch below the graph).
doc_op_events: Events: a column header sorts, “the 200/1000 strongest” loads more.
doc_op_sensitivity: Sensitivity 0.3 to 0.7 per profile and per recording; 0.5 is the calibrated point. A change re-analyzes.
doc_op_fixed_gain: Fixed level (profile): USB turntables without a level control get no gain hints.
doc_op_system: System (tab): running and queued analyses, CPU, memory, temperature. The pill at the top right opens the same list.
doc_limits_p: The grade limits are not calibrated; anchor points by ear are being collected. The noise depends on the chain. The deck baseline is only valid as long as the test record was clean during setup. In pink noise and dense cymbal passages every detector is blind or noisy; the audit is the way to measure that.
